---
title: "Trump trade policy 2.0"
description: "A chronicle of the administration's early trade moves since January 21 — investigations before sweeping tariffs, mixed signals on China, and internal debate over a universal tariff."
date: "2025-03-04"
categories: [trade-wars]
---

This post traces the administration's trade actions from January 21, 2025
onward: an initial focus on investigations into trade deficits and unfair
practices rather than immediate sweeping tariffs, threats of 25% tariffs on
Canada and Mexico (with a possible oil exemption), a comparatively softer
line on China with a proposed 10% tariff tied to fentanyl, and a brief tariff
threat against Colombia that was quickly withdrawn. It also flags an internal
administration split — Treasury Secretary Bessent floated phasing in a
universal tariff at 2.5% a month, while Trump pushed for larger, faster
increases.

**Originally published on Substack**, March 4, 2025.
